Gradient is monotonic with distance from the vessel and reconciles with the stated mechanism: 3 at the nearest cottage, 5 halfway, 11 at the far bungalow.
justification: C is the definition given verbatim: “The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air: the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything”. A inverts the gradient: the sheet reads “three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow”, so the figures RISE as the warning weakens, and eleven is the worst reading on the run rather than a good one. B mistakes the method for the datum; the quarter-turn is how he walks the dilution up, since he “opens its needle valve a quarter-turn at a time and sniffs at the funnel until the smell arrives”, while what is written down is the dilution the box reports. D makes the figure a calculation from pipe length, but it is a nose measurement taken house by house: “The box is honest about the dilution and silent about the nose”. Length explains the slope; it does not produce the number.

justification: A restates the passage directly: “Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells” - partly changed, and the product is near odourless. B is contradicted by “put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume”. C is the near miss and dies on its time clause: the oxide is already present before service, being “a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard”; the taking is worst at the very start, since “a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service”; and corrosion with age works the other way, because “Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking”. So C's requirement that the steel has begun to corrode in service reverses the passage's own order of events. D is contradicted by “the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in”.

Arithmetic reconciles with real combustion data: propane's lower flammable limit is about 2.1 vol% = 21 parts per thousand parts of air, and a fifth of that is 4.2, i.e. the stated working figure of four.
The post-soak re-walk reads six, still above four, so the soak is correctly shown as unfinished; option B's word 'second' is looser than 'walking the run again' but creates no rival answer.
justification: B is the only option not contradicted, and it tracks “The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again”: the end is set by re-measurement, not by a date. A fails twice, against “holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose until it will take no more” and against “What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance”. C inverts the economics: “one call-out to a kitchen where the cooker is off and the smell is only the soak costs more than the odorant does”. D is contradicted by “you do it before the first burner is lit”. Noted but not disqualifying: B's word second is looser than the passage, since the re-walk actually shown ends “The figure he writes down is six”, still above the working figure of four, so the soak is not over and further walks may be needed. Read as another walk, which is what walking the run again means, B stands and no rival option survives.

Mileages reconcile exactly: 9 miles Haddenthorpe-Nerresby plus 21 miles beyond Haddenthorpe = the stated 30 miles Nerresby-Thrapmere.
Geometry is consistent: the Shenwolds are 4 miles from Haddenthorpe and 3 miles off a road running through Haddenthorpe (3 < 4).
Dates are load-bearing and consistent: the 1227 charter predates the 1769 turnpike by 542 years, which is what licenses A over B.
justification: Every card day lands on a market day. “Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long”, and “Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday”. The 1227 charter predates the turnpike by 542 years, so the market days, not the road, set the order of the week: A. B is the attribution the essay undercuts, since “The circuit has been put down to the coach road, turnpiked in 1769” is reported and then falsified by the Shenwolds appearing on the card even though “The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use”. C is killed by “Upper Shenwold has no market of its own”, the pairing being the ten minute walk rather than two markets. D is killed by “the Thursday market is the largest of the four”. The mileages reconcile: nine miles Haddenthorpe to Nerresby plus twenty-one beyond Haddenthorpe equals the stated thirty to Thrapmere.

Bokstavsantalen summerar exakt: 1+2+3+5+6+7+8+8 = 40 pa atta rader, som angivet.

Det nya arkets storleksstege sluter sig exakt pa sin egen identitet: 73 mm overst, faktor 20 over 14 rader ger 73/20 = 3,65 mm (knappt fyra), en radkvot pa 20^(1/13) = 1,259 (ungefar en fjardedel storre), och 7,27/3,65 = 1,99 alltsa visus 2,0. justification: Texten ger stegen rakt ut: ”Den översta bokstaven är 73 millimeter, nästa rad 36 och den därefter 24.” Det översta steget är alltså ett fall på 37 mm, drygt hälften, medan det understa är 0,8 mm.
